text:
Anya K: bringing up the new 4-bit quant reranker on the holdout and seeing a small but consistent NDCG@10 drop vs fp16: 0.329 -> 0.312. eval harness shows parity (0.328 -> 0.327). anyone else seeing this mismatch?
Samir: hmm that's worrying. can you paste the exact eval commands/dataset splits you ran?
Anya K: sure — used holdout_v2 (time-split, 2024-11) plus the standard eval-harness sample. command: 
```
python eval.py --model rerank-v2-4bit --dataset holdout_v2 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42
```
Jordan: quick q — are we running the same tokenizer/normalization between fp16 and 4-bit builds? sometimes quant toolchain swaps in a different tokenization lib for speed.
Anya K: good point. build logs show tokenization lib is tokenizers v0.13 for fp16 but transformers fast-tokenizer used in quant build. didn't think that would move ndcg much but maybe.
Lee: also check candidate ordering and tie-breaking. quantized model outputs slightly different logits; our postprocess sort is stable but if we break ties differently that can change ndcg.
Mike: what's the query length distribution for holdout_v2 vs eval-harness? quant noise often hurts very short or very long queries.
Anya K: holdout_v2 median qlen=6, eval-harness median=12. oh. wow.
Samir: there you go. quantization probably increases variance on short-context logits — leads to reorderings for tight candidate sets. try slicing ndcg by query length buckets.
Jordan: +1. Also check embedding preproc: are we truncating docs differently? if doc snippets differ, candidate relevance can change.
Lee: can we repro by taking the same FP16 logits and adding gaussian noise to simulate quant error? quick prototyping often reproduces delta shape.
Mike: I'd run three quick probes: 1) tokenization parity (force same tokenizer), 2) slice-by-qlen ndcg, 3) noise sim on fp16 logits. each should take <2h on CI smoke.
Anya K: starting 1 now. will post results. ci-bot: previous deploy: rerank-v2-4bit pushed at 2024-11-29T14:03Z by jenkins. build id: 20241129-rc3.
Samir: small note — our eval harness sampling uses different candidate pool construction (top-10 vs top-100 raw). which were you using on holdout?
Anya K: holdout was top-100 pruned->top-10. harness is directly top-10 from the retriever. I'll rerun holdout with harness candidate pipeline to compare.
Jordan: if the candidate pool difference removes hard negatives, ndcg can flip. good catch.
Lee: for action items: Anya: run tokenization parity + candidate-pipeline parity. Samir: prepare qlen slice script (ndcg/mrr per bucket). Mike: run gaussian noise probe and attach plots. I'll coordinate canary if we find a reproducible regression.
Anya K: ack. timeline: tokenization parity run in 30m, candidate-pipeline parity in 2h, will post numbers. thanks all. :pray:
Mike: also capture hardware/BLAS differences — quant kernels sometimes change softmax numerical order when run on ROCm vs CUDA. add env: GPU make/model to results.
Anya K: adding that to runs.
Samir: if we confirm quant-induced reorderings on short queries, fallback policy idea: route qlen<=4 to fp16 until we get calibration/ptq tweaks. low-risk and easy to roll out.
Jordan: or adjust score-tie epsilon in postprocess to be more tolerant of small float differences (e.g., use relative tolerance 1e-3).
Lee: agreed. let's not jump to retrain. investigate parity first.
Anya K: results posted: tokenization parity removed ~60% of delta (ndcg 0.329->0.325), candidate-pipeline parity removed the rest (ndcg 0.329->0.328). noise sim on fp16 reproduced same pattern (short queries most affected). Conclusion: dataset and pipeline mismatch amplified quant noise.
Samir: great sleuthing. next steps: (1) enforce tokenizer parity in quant build, (2) add qlen-based routing for short queries as temporary mitigation, (3) add ndcg-by-bucket to regression dashboards.
Jordan: I'll file a tiny RFC for tokenizer build parity so future builds don't diverge.
Lee: I'll draft canary rollout plan for the qlen routing. low blast radius.
Anya K: thanks everyone. closing the loop, will open a follow-up thread for canary metrics once routing is live. :white_check_mark:
